title: Comfort Club Enrollment Eligibility: Qualifying Systems, Equipment Age and Inspection
content:
Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements enroll heating and cooling systems only. The eligibility basis below applies at enrollment and equally to a system added to an agreement mid-term.

## Eligibility basis

1. **Registered and in service.** Every system enrolled must be an equipment unit registered at the customer's address whose equipment status is in service. The equipment register is the authority, checked before the system is enrolled.
2. **Heating or cooling unit.** It must be a central air conditioner, heat pump, gas furnace, air handler, ductless mini-split or boiler. A tank water heater is never enrolled as a system; on tiers with whole-home visits the water heater is serviced on the whole-home visit instead.
3. **Paired units.** An indoor unit and the outdoor unit it is paired with count as one system.
4. **Age limit.** Each enrolled system must be no older than the tier's oldest equipment age accepted on the enrollment date: the enrollment date must not be later than the equipment's install date plus that number of years. The limit is counted in calendar months — the number of years times twelve, added to the install date; when that day does not exist in the resulting month, the boundary falls on the last day of that month. An enrollment dated exactly on the boundary is accepted.
5. **Enrollment inspection.** A system older than the tier's inspection threshold but within the age limit is enrolled only with an enrollment inspection, billed once per inspected system as an enrollment inspection fee charge at the tier's enrollment inspection fee. A fee of 0.00 means the inspection is performed without charge and no fee entry is posted.
6. **System count.** The number of systems enrolled — at enrollment or by adding a system — may not exceed the tier's maximum number of systems covered. A customer with more systems enrolls the ones they choose or takes a tier with a higher limit.
7. **Systems added mid-term.** The same age limit and inspection rule apply to a system added mid-term, measured on the date it is added.
8. **Opening the agreement.** Enrollment opens the agreement in pending status. The term starts on the enrollment date and ends one day before the same calendar date a term length later, and the count of consecutive terms is set to 1.

## Age-limit boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Install date | Age limit on the tier | Boundary date | Enrollment on | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 June 2010 | 15 years | 15 June 2025 | 15 June 2025 | Accepted (on the boundary) |
| 15 June 2010 | 15 years | 15 June 2025 | 16 June 2025 | Refused (later than the boundary) |
| 29 February 2000 | 25 years | 28 February 2025 (29 February does not exist in 2025) | 28 February 2025 | Accepted |
| 29 February 2000 | 25 years | 28 February 2025 | 1 March 2025 | Refused |

## Term dates (hypothetical)
An agreement enrolled on 10 March 2025 on a 12-month term opens pending, with the term running from 10 March 2025 to 9 March 2026 and a consecutive term count of 1.

## Points of judgement
- A boiler and a ductless mini-split at the same address are two systems; an air handler and the condenser it is paired with are one.
- A tank water heater is not a system for the count, whatever the tier.
